Gujarat.text: B.Arch admission is run by the Admission Committee for Professional Courses (ACPC Gujarat), which uses NATA scores (plus JEE Main Paper 2 in the merit); the 2026-27 B.Arch online programme opened 19 May 2026. Private universities such as Nirma reserve about 15% seats as NRI/NRI-sponsored (fee in USD) and fill the rest via ACPC and All India categories; UTU describes 25% Management/NRI quota filled on merit under ACPC procedure (older page).

Goa.text: Goa College of Architecture (Altinho, Panaji) is a government college affiliated to Goa University with intake of 60 B.Arch seats including seats for other states (Goa govt page). Admission is understood to be NATA-based via DTE Goa (2026 notice exists at dte.goa.gov.in but could not be read); no NRI rule verified.

Puducherry.text: Government-quota B.Arch seats (50%) are allotted by the Centralized Admission Committee (CENTAC) and management-quota seats (50%) through the private colleges' association test (CETPPEC); merit uses 50% NATA/JEE Architecture score and 50% qualifying-exam marks, as stated in the Sri Manakula Vinayagar admission procedure sheet. CENTAC invited B.Arch applications in July 2025.

Jharkhand.text: BIT Mesra admits B.Arch both through JoSAA/CSAB (JEE Main Paper 2) and its own NATA-score round (2025 guidelines dated 2 July 2025).
